tables.name: payments
tables.description: Synthetic dataset of payment transactions processed by a payment processor. Each row represents one transaction.

columns.name: psp_reference
columns.description: Unique payment identifier.

columns.name: merchant
columns.description: Merchant name.

columns.name: card_scheme
columns.description: Card scheme (network) used for the transaction.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Year of payment initiation. Always 2023 in this dataset.

columns.name: hour_of_day
columns.description: Hour of the day of payment initiation (0-23).

columns.name: minute_of_hour
columns.description: Minute of the hour of payment initiation (0-59).

columns.name: day_of_year
columns.description: Day of the year of payment initiation (1-365).

columns.name: month
columns.description: Month of payment initiation (1-12).

columns.name: is_credit
columns.description: Whether the card used is a credit card. FALSE indicates a debit card. Credit transactions are typically more expensive.

columns.name: eur_amount
columns.description: Payment amount in euros.

columns.name: ip_country
columns.description: Country the shopper was in at the time of the transaction, determined by IP address. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

columns.name: issuing_country
columns.description: Country of the card-issuing bank. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. When this matches acquirer_country, the transaction is domestic (intracountry).

columns.name: device_type
columns.description: Device type used for the transaction.

columns.name: ip_address
columns.description: Hashed shopper IP address.

columns.name: email_address
columns.description: Hashed shopper email address. May be empty.

columns.name: card_number
columns.description: Hashed card number.

columns.name: shopper_interaction
columns.description: Payment method.

columns.name: card_bin
columns.description: Bank Identification Number (first digits of card number).

columns.name: has_fraudulent_dispute
columns.description: Whether the issuing bank flagged the transaction as a fraudulent dispute.

columns.name: is_refused_by_adyen
columns.description: Whether the transaction was refused by Adyen.

columns.name: aci
columns.description: Authorization Characteristics Indicator. Identifies how the transaction was submitted to the acquirer.

value_labels.D: Card not present, card on file

columns.name: acquirer_country
columns.description: Country of the acquiring bank. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

tables.name: acquirer_countries
tables.description: Lookup table mapping acquirer names to their country codes.

columns.name: acquirer
columns.description: Name of the acquiring bank.

columns.name: country_code
columns.description: Country of the acquirer. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

tables.name: merchants
tables.description: Merchant profiles with business classification and processing configuration. Each row represents one merchant.

columns.name: merchant
columns.description: Merchant name.

columns.name: capture_delay
columns.description: Capture delay range. Faster capture is generally more expensive.

columns.name: merchant_category_code
columns.description: Four-digit Merchant Category Code classifying the business type.

columns.name: account_type
columns.description: Business model classification.

tables.name: merchant_acquirers
tables.description: Junction table linking merchants to their acquiring banks. A merchant may route transactions through multiple acquirers (typically in different countries) to enable local acquiring.

columns.name: merchant
columns.description: Merchant name.

columns.name: acquirer
columns.description: Name of the acquiring bank.

tables.name: fees
tables.description: Fee rules for payment processing. Each row is a rule with constraints that determine which transactions it applies to. A rule matches a transaction when all non-null fields match. Null (scalar) or empty (list) means "matches all values." The fee for a matched transaction is: fixed_amount + rate * eur_amount / 10000.

columns.name: ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for the fee rule.

columns.name: card_scheme
columns.description: Card scheme this rule applies to. Always set (never null).

columns.name: capture_delay
columns.description: Capture delay range this rule applies to. Null means all. Matches the same enum used in the merchants table.

columns.name: fraud_percent_min
columns.description: Minimum monthly fraud level (%) this rule applies to (inclusive). -Inf means no lower bound, and is by far the most common value (926 of 1000 rules); the finite values observed run from 7.2 to 8.3.

columns.name: fraud_percent_max
columns.description: Maximum monthly fraud level (%) this rule applies to (exclusive). Inf means no upper bound, and is by far the most common value (921 of 1000 rules); the finite values observed run from 7.2 to 8.3.

columns.name: monthly_volume
columns.description: Monthly transaction volume range this rule applies to. Null means all.

columns.name: is_credit
columns.description: Whether this rule applies to credit (TRUE) or debit (FALSE) transactions. Null means both.

columns.name: fixed_amount
columns.description: Fixed fee component (also called "absolute fee") in euros per transaction.

columns.name: rate
columns.description: Variable fee rate (also called "relative fee"). Multiply by transaction value and divide by 10000 to get the variable component in euros.

columns.name: intracountry
columns.description: Whether this rule applies to domestic (TRUE) or international (FALSE) transactions. A transaction is domestic when issuing_country equals acquirer_country. Null means both.

tables.name: merchant_months
tables.description: Monthly aggregates per merchant, computed from the payments data. Used for matching payments to fee rules based on monthly fraud level and transaction volume thresholds.

columns.name: merchant
columns.description: Merchant name.

columns.name: year
columns.description: Year.

columns.name: total_volume
columns.description: Total transaction volume in euros for this merchant-month.

columns.name: fraud_volume
columns.description: Total volume of transactions flagged as fraudulent disputes, in euros.

columns.name: fraud_percent
columns.description: Fraud rate as a percentage: fraud_volume / total_volume * 100.

columns.name: monthly_volume
columns.description: Binned total_volume matching the fee rule volume ranges.

tables.name: merchant_category_codes
tables.description: Lookup table of Merchant Category Codes (MCCs). MCCs are four-digit codes assigned by card networks to classify a merchant's business type.

columns.name: mcc
columns.description: Four-digit Merchant Category Code.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Human-readable description of the merchant category.

relationships.description: Each merchant has one or more acquirers.
Each merchant has monthly aggregates for each active month.
Each merchant has one merchant category code.

glossary.definition: The acquiring bank that processes a merchant's card transactions and settles funds. Also called the "acquiring bank" or "merchant bank."
The card network (e.g. GlobalCard, NexPay) that sets rules and interchange rates for transactions on its network.
Authorization Characteristics Indicator. A code that identifies the transaction flow submitted to the acquirer (e.g. card-present vs card-not-present, authenticated vs non-authenticated).
Merchant Category Code. A four-digit code assigned by card networks to classify a merchant's business type, used for risk assessment, fraud detection, and fee determination.
A domestic transaction where the card-issuing country and the acquiring country are the same. Intracountry transactions typically have lower fees than cross-border transactions.
Bank Identification Number. The first six to eight digits of a card number that identify the issuing bank.
Point of Sale. An in-person or in-store transaction, as opposed to an online (ecommerce) transaction.
A payment security protocol that adds an extra authentication step for online card-not-present transactions, reducing fraud risk.
A reversal of a transaction initiated by the cardholder's issuing bank, typically due to a dispute or fraud claim.
The number of days between authorization and settlement of a transaction. Faster capture is generally more expensive.
